clue.text: Competent assistant cuts wire

indicators.note: something that cuts into a word splits it and sits inside the gap

blocks.note: a cable is an insulated wire
PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A capable helper snips through a wire, perhaps defusing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' suggests snipping, but here the assistant splits the wire word and sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable and competent are synonyms, both describing someone able to do a job well.

clue.text: Hot wash runs after cold programme

indicators.note: colours that run in the wash bleed and mix, so the letters are jumbled
placing one piece after another fixes their order in the answer

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A laundry mishap: a hot wash makes colours run after a cold one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like washing-machine instructions; 'runs' is the colour-bleeding sense, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat show is a type of television programme built around interviews with guests.

clue.text: French film company of course European

blocks.note: a path is a course or route
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A French film company that is, naturally, European.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathé is a long-established French film production and distribution company, famous for its newsreels.

clue.text: Rabbit that's divided for burger

blocks.note: first meaning: a pet name or dialect word for a rabbit, as in bunny
second meaning: the bread roll split in two to hold a burger

explanation.surface: A rabbit being cut up for a burger, a grim menu item.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests butchery; in fact the second half describes the bread roll sliced open around a patty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bun is an informal name for a rabbit, and also the soft roll that is sliced open to hold a burger.

clue.text: Earth dead? Cheer up

blocks.note: E is an abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about the planet's death, followed by a brisk instruction to cheer up.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with high spirits, which is a transitive way of saying to cheer someone up.

clue.text: Witch costume for TV returned looking the worse for wear

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
TV is short for transvestite, whose costume is drag

explanation.surface: A witch costume sent back to the TV wardrobe department because it looks tatty.
explanation.walkthrough: TV is not television here but the old abbreviation for transvestite, whose costume is the one turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard describes a face looking exhausted and worn, as if from fatigue or worry.

clue.text: US lawyer uncovered case of youth uprising in state capital

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its two end letters are kept
in a down entry, rising up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a DA is a District Attorney in the US
bared means stripped of covering
the first and last letters of youth

explanation.surface: A US lawyer exposes a case concerning a youth uprising in some state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' and 'uprising' read as legal and political nouns, but one keeps the outside letters and the other turns the down entry upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyderabad is the capital city of the Indian state of Telangana.

clue.text: Gross affluence meets demonstration stopping oil

blocks.note: gr. is an abbreviation for gross
ease is comfort and affluence, as in a life of ease
a proof is a demonstration that something is true

explanation.surface: Vulgar wealth confronts a protest blockading an oil pipeline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopping oil' reads like a protest's aim, but it is the definition: the paper that grease cannot get through.
explanation.definitionFit: Greaseproof paper resists fat and oil soaking through it, so it stops oil.

clue.text: Gas surprisingly clean yet ultimately non-renewable

indicators.note: a surprising result is an unexpected arrangement, so these letters are reworked
ultimately points to the last letter of the following word only

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the final letter of non-renewable

explanation.surface: An energy-policy remark about a fuel that burns clean but cannot be renewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used in welding torches.

clue.text: How awful finding limb in river

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A horrified reaction to discovering a severed limb in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear me is an exclamation of dismay, used just like how awful.

clue.text: Working tea lady with apron on can't play

indicators.note: something working is in operation, shaken into action, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: part of the letters to be rearranged
the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tea lady at work in her apron is unable to perform a role on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb about being unable to act; it is a noun naming the Shakespeare tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony and Cleopatra is a tragedy by Shakespeare, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: Injection treatment partly using same needles in recession

indicators.note: partly means only part of the following words is used, sitting inside them
something in recession goes backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: letters running across same and needles

explanation.surface: A worry about clinics reusing needles for injections during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recession' sounds economic but just signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is liquid injected into the rectum as a medical treatment.

clue.text: Mini in street brought to suit couple

indicators.note: one word placed in another is put inside it

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
wee means tiny, mini
hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A Mini car parked in the street is brought round to suit a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Mini looks like the car but means small; wee is Scottish and informal for little.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of sweethearts are two people romantically attached, which is a couple.

clue.text: Article captain holds on sailing ship

indicators.note: a word that holds something has it inside

blocks.note: the is the definite article
re means on, concerning
the master is the captain of a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a captain aboard a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-master is a sailing vessel with three masts.

clue.text: From behind, Juan's very tasty!

indicators.note: reading from behind means starting at the end, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: muy is Spanish for very, the word a Juan would use

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing Juan from behind and approving loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Juan stands for a Spanish speaker, so his very is the Spanish word, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yum is an exclamation said about delicious food, so it works as an interjection meaning tasty.

clue.text: Fellow leaves first of two shellfish

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer there, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the former is the first of two things mentioned
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: One of two people departs first, leaving the shellfish behind.
explanation.walkthrough: FORMER loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an abalone, an edible mollusc found around the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Tiny male spider, say, causing hiatus at concert

blocks.note: mini means tiny
M is the abbreviation for male
in snooker a spider is a kind of rest for the cue

explanation.surface: A tiny male spider crawls on stage and halts a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The spider is not the animal: in snooker it is a raised cue support, one of several kinds of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim rest is a musical notation for a silence lasting two beats, a pause in a performance.

clue.text: Jazz musician possibly bitter accepting work in oil company

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so it goes inside
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: bitter is a kind of beer, hence possibly
op is short for opus, a work
BP is a major oil company

explanation.surface: A jazz player, perhaps embittered, takes a job at an oil firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British draught ale, so 'possibly' marks it as an example of the drink; the work goes into the company, and both go into the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A bebopper is a player of bebop, a fast, complex style of jazz.

clue.text: Train service runs after strike, more or less

indicators.note: placing one piece after another fixes their order in the answer

blocks.note: to buffet is to strike repeatedly
ca. is circa, meaning approximately
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rail service resumes running after a strike, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The rail-strike picture is a decoy; train service is the definition, a carriage serving food.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet car is a railway carriage where refreshments are served, a service on a train.

clue.text: See great changes in cheap accommodation

indicators.note: the letters undergo changes, being rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Budget travellers notice big improvements in their lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship, the lowest-priced berths.

clue.text: On short rations as commanded by Iron Duke

blocks.note: under someone means commanded by them
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Troops serving under the Iron Duke, Wellington, going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Duke was the Duke of Wellington's nickname, but here iron and duke are separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Underfed means given too little food, which is what being on short rations amounts to.

clue.text: Deliveries trainee's left in full view

indicators.note: the leftmost end of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
the first letter of trainee

explanation.surface: A trainee bowler's deliveries have been left out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled; left here means the left-hand end, not departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and not concealed, plainly visible to everyone.

clue.text: Perishing with convulsive twitch after electrical discharge

indicators.note: placing one piece after another fixes their order in the answer

blocks.note: an arc is a luminous electrical discharge
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone dying, twitching convulsively after an electric shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Perishing reads as dying but is the British colloquial sense of bitterly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishing is British slang for extremely cold, the same idea as arctic used loosely.

clue.text: Old Russian satellite turns in outermost circle

indicators.note: something that turns faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station

explanation.surface: An old Russian space station orbiting in the outermost ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rim is the outer edge of something round, its outermost circle.

clue.text: Answer magazine's boss gives prematurely

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
Time is a news magazine, and its boss is its head

explanation.surface: A magazine editor responds too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine is Time, so the head of Time is its boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead of time means before the expected moment, which is what prematurely means.

clue.text: Leaving university, compulsion becomes habit

indicators.note: whatever is leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: duress is compulsion by threats
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: After leaving college, a compulsion hardens into a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit is not a routine but clothing, such as a nun's or riding habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a distinctive garment, such as a monk's robe, so it is a kind of dress.

clue.text: Lead in paint Rothko has absorbed

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside, so the answer sits within the words

blocks.note: letters running across paint and Rothko

explanation.surface: Mark Rothko's paint has soaked up lead, a toxic pigment.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead looks like the metal in paint; it is the verb-noun sense of an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening of a song or article, which is the lead-in or lead.

clue.text: Sound chirpy pretty close to defeat

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: twee means overly pretty or quaint
the last letter of defeat

explanation.surface: Someone sounding cheerful when they are on the verge of losing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweet is to make the high chirping call of a small bird.

clue.text: See 9
A year ending in December is what you'd expect

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter, the only one used

blocks.note: p.a. is per annum, meaning a year
the final letter of December

explanation.surface: A year that finishes in December is just the normal state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or expected standard, as in 'par for the course'.

clue.text: Whip near Keir regularly is party manager

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a cat o' nine tails is a whip
the even letters of near Keir

explanation.surface: The party whip, sitting near Keir Starmer, runs the party.
explanation.walkthrough: Whip and party suggest Labour politics around Keir Starmer, but the party is a social one with food.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies and manages the food and drink for a party or event.

clue.text: Employer of Bob Marley visits

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who hires the reggae star Bob Marley when he comes calling
setter's reading: in A Christmas Carol, the boss of Bob Cratchit, who is visited by the ghost of Jacob Marley

explanation.surface: Someone who employs the reggae singer Bob Marley on his tours.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob and Marley are separate: Bob Cratchit is the clerk, and Marley is the dead partner whose ghost visits on Christmas Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's A Christmas Carol the miser employs clerk Bob Cratchit and is haunted by his former partner Marley.
